outlooks.summary: BANDS OF THUNDERSTORMS -- SOME OF WHICH WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING DAMAGING WINDS AND POSSIBLY A COUPLE OF TORNADOES -- ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP DURING THE AFTERNOON FROM IOWA SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO EASTERN TEXAS. THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS SHOULD RESIDE ACROSS PARTS OF SOUTHERN IOWA...NORTHERN MISSOURI...AND INTO NORTHERN AND CENTRAL ILLINOIS.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS A MID-LEVEL SHORT-WAVE TROUGH DEPARTS NEW ENGLAND EARLY IN THE PERIOD...A STRONGLY DYNAMIC TROUGH/LOW WILL EJECT QUICKLY EWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH THE DAY...AND THEN ENEWD ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST AND INTO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES/OH VALLEY STATES THROUGH THE END OF THE PERIOD. THIS SYSTEM WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY INTENSE FLOW ALOFT...INCLUDING A 60 KT SLY LOW-LEVEL JET AHEAD OF THE SYSTEM AND A 100-PLUS KT SWLY MID-LEVEL JET STREAK SE OF THE DEVELOPING LOW. AT THE SURFACE...A STEADILY DEEPENING LOW -- INITIALLY OVER KS -- WILL PROGRESS ENEWD TO WI LATE. THE TRAILING COLD FRONT WHICH WILL BE CROSSING WRN PORTIONS OF THE SRN PLAINS AT THE START OF THE PERIOD...WILL ACCELERATE QUICKLY EWD...MOVING ACROSS WRN MO/WRN AR/ERN OK AND ERN TX THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING AND THEN ACROSS THE MS/OH/TN VALLEYS THROUGH THE LATTER HALF OF THE PERIOD. THIS SYSTEM WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY SHOWERS AND SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS...AND ASSOCIATED RISK FOR LOCAL WIND DAMAGE AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES.

sections.title: IA/IL/INDIANA VICINITY SSWWD TO NRN LA/E TX
sections.text: SHOWERS AND EMBEDDED/ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS ARE FORECAST TO SPREAD ACROSS THE MID MO VALLEY REGION EARLY IN THE PERIOD...AS A STRONG STORM SYSTEM CROSSES THE CENTRAL PLAINS. BY MID AFTERNOON...DEVELOPMENT OF CONVECTION IS FORECAST ALONG THE SHARP/FAST-MOVING COLD FRONT...WITHIN A MARGINALLY MOIST/MODESTLY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR. ATTM...IT APPEARS THAT THE BOUNDARY LAYER -- PARTICULARLY FROM THE ARKLATEX REGION NWD -- MAY REMAIN SLIGHTLY STABLE THROUGH FROPA. THIS COMBINED WITH THE OVERALL MEAGER/LOW-TOPPED CAPE SUGGESTS THAT CONVECTION WILL STRUGGLE TO BECOME ORGANIZED/SUSTAINED...WITH THE EXTREMELY STRONG WIND SHEAR SPREADING ACROSS THE REGION POSSIBLY BEING A DETRIMENT IN THIS CASE TO WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION. WHERE STORMS CAN BE SUSTAINED -- AND THUS ABLE TO UTILIZE THE STRONGLY SHEARED ENVIRONMENT...UPDRAFT ROTATION AND ATTENDANT RISK FOR A TORNADO OR TWO WILL RESULT. ADDITIONALLY...LOCAL UPSCALE GROWTH INTO FAST-MOVING BANDS OF CONVECTION WILL RESULT IN POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING WINDS. THE MOST FAVORABLE CORRIDOR FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND ISOLATED TORNADOES APPEARS ATTM TO RESIDE ACROSS THE SRN IA/NRN MO/NWRN IL VICINITY...ALONG THE PATH OF THE UPPER SYSTEM AND JUST AHEAD OF

outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP DURING THE AFTERNOON ACROSS PARTS OF THE MISSOURI VALLEY SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO EASTERN TEXAS. THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING SHOULD EXIST ACROSS PARTS OF IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI INTO NORTHERN AND CENTRAL ILLINOIS.

sections.title: THERE IS AN ENH RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF IA/MO/IL
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE MO VALLEY/MIDWEST SOUTHWARD TO THE ARKLATEX... ...THERE IS A MRGL RISK OF SVR TSTMS SURROUNDING THE ENH/SLGT RISK AREAS...

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A DEEP UPPER TROUGH CENTERED OVER THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN ROCKIES AND ADJACENT HIGH PLAINS EARLY THIS MORNING WILL ACCELERATE EAST-NORTHEASTWARD OVER THE PLAINS TODAY AND REACH THE UPPER GREAT LAKES BY LATE TONIGHT/EARLY THURSDAY. THIS SYSTEM IS BEING ACCOMPANIED BY VERY STRONG DEEP-TROPOSPHERIC FLOW...HIGHLIGHTED BY A 100-130 KT MID/HIGH-LEVEL SOUTHWESTERLY JET WITH AN INCREASINGLY STRONG /50-75 KT/ LOW-LEVEL JET INTO TONIGHT. STEADY SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS WILL CONTINUE TO OCCUR OVER KS EARLY TODAY...WITH THE SURFACE LOW DEEPENING NORTHEASTWARD INTO IA/WI THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. A COLD FRONT ACROSS THE SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS EARLY TODAY WILL ACCELERATE GENERALLY EASTWARD...REACHING THE OH/TN RIVER VALLEYS AND LOWER MS VALLEY/COASTAL TX LATE TONIGHT/EARLY THURSDAY.

sections.title: MO VALLEY/MIDWEST INCLUDING IA/MO/IL/SOUTHERN WI
sections.text: IN SPITE OF AMPLE MOISTURE FLUXES TODAY...MARGINAL MOISTURE QUALITY INTO THE REGION SHOULD PRECLUDE WHAT WOULD OTHERWISE LIKELY BE A MORE CONSEQUENTIAL SEVERE WEATHER RISK IN THE PRESENCE OF ROBUST FORCING FOR ASCENT/VERTICAL SHEAR. NONETHELESS...SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS INCLUDING THE POTENTIAL FOR WIND DAMAGE AND A FEW TORNADOES CAN BE EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT WITHIN A HIGHLY SHEARED/WEAKLY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT. WITH THE LOW-LEVEL MOIST AXIS EXTENDING FROM OK INTO EAST-CENTRAL KS/NORTHWEST MO EARLY THIS MORNING...A NARROW CORRIDOR OF 50S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY ESTABLISHED THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE REGION...RESULTING IN A MODESTLY MOIST/UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR NEAR/AHEAD OF THE DEEPENING SURFACE CYCLONE AND THE EASTWARD-ACCELERATING COLD FRONT. VARIOUS CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODELS SUCH AS EARLY-MORNING HRRR/HRRR-ESRL RUNS AND 00Z WRF-NSSL SUGGEST THAT INITIAL SURFACE-BASED STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT...LIKELY AS SEMI-DISCRETE LOW-TOPPED STORMS...MAY OCCUR AS EARLY AS NOON-2PM CST NEAR THE MISSOURI RIVER ACROSS SOUTHWEST/SOUTH-CENTRAL IA AND NORTHERN MO. LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE/BUOYANCY IN THE PRESENCE OF 200+ 0-1 KM SRH SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR A F

sections.title: MID-SOUTH/OZARKS/ARKLATEX/EAST TX
sections.text: ISOLATED/WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS MAY BEGIN TO DEVELOP/GRADUALLY INTENSIFY BY EARLY/MID-AFTERNOON...INITIALLY WITHIN A CORRIDOR SPANNING FAR SOUTHERN MO...FAR SOUTHEAST OK...AND WESTERN/CENTRAL AR SOUTHWESTWARD TO NORTHEAST/EAST TX. THIS DEVELOPMENT SHOULD OCCUR WITHIN A MODESTLY MOIST/UNSTABLE PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR AMID WEAK LOW-LEVEL CONFLUENCE. EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-55 KT WOULD SUPPORT SOME SUPERCELLS. WHILE WINDS IN THE 1-3 KM AGL LAYER WILL BE TENDING TO VEER THIS AFTERNOON...SUFFICIENT SPEED SHEAR COULD YIELD A TORNADO ASIDE FROM ISOLATED WIND DAMAGE. WHILE A FEW INSTANCES OF SEVERE HAIL MAY BE POSSIBLE THROUGH MID/LATE AFTERNOON...THE OVERALL HAIL POTENTIAL SHOULD BE TEMPERED BY WEAK MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. ..GUYER/MARSH.. 11/11/2015

outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP DURING THE AFTERNOON ACROSS PARTS OF THE MISSOURI VALLEY SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO EASTERN TEXAS. THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING SHOULD EXIST ACROSS PARTS OF IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI INTO NORTHERN AND CENTRAL ILLINOIS.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A STRONG MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL PROGRESS ENEWD FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS TO THE MID MS VALLEY BY THIS EVENING...AND CONTINUE TO THE GREAT LAKES/OH VALLEY OVERNIGHT. AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE CYCLONE IN N CENTRAL KS AS OF LATE MORNING WILL DEVELOP NEWD TO CENTRAL IA THIS EVENING AND WI OVERNIGHT...AS A REMNANT LEE TROUGH/DRYLINE MOVES EWD FROM KS/OK TO MO/WRN AR...BEFORE BEING OVERTAKEN BY THE SURFACE COLD FRONT THIS EVENING. LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IS SPREADING NWD/NEWD FROM E TX IN THE WARM SECTOR...THOUGH THE RICHER MOISTURE WILL LIKELY REMAIN SOMEWHAT DISPLACED FROM THE STEEPER LAPSE RATES CLOSER TO THE SURFACE LOW AND MIDLEVEL TROUGH. THUS...THE SEVERE STORM RISK SHOULD BE RELATIVELY GREATER CLOSER TO THE SURFACE CYCLONE...AND FARTHER S WHERE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE/BUOYANCY WILL BE LARGEST ACROSS NE TX.

sections.title: IA/NRN MO/WRN IL THROUGH THIS EVENING
sections.text: THE SURFACE CYCLONE IN N CENTRAL KS WILL DEVELOP NEWD ALONG A STALLED FRONT TOWARD CENTRAL IA THIS EVENING. 12Z SOUNDINGS SHOWED THE STEEPEST MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ALONG AND JUST N OF THE MIDLEVEL JET CORE...AND THIS AREA WILL COINCIDE WITH THE N EDGE OF THE RETURNING LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE /BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS 55-60 F/. FOCUSED FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL SPREAD NEWD IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE SURFACE LOW/MIDLEVEL TROUGH...REACHING EXTREME NE KS/SE NEB/SW IA/NW MO BY AROUND 18Z. SURFACE-BASED CONVECTIVE INITIATION IS EXPECTED IN THE 18-20Z TIME FRAME IN A NW-SE ARC CLOSE TO THE MO RIVER FROM KANSAS CITY TO OMAHA...WITH STORMS EXPECTED TO SPREAD QUICKLY EWD THROUGH THE AFTERNOON/EVENING ACROSS NRN MO/SRN IA. THOUGH MOISTURE AND BUOYANCY WILL NOT BE PARTICULARLY LARGE...VERTICAL SHEAR WILL FAVOR A BROKEN BAND OF LOW-TOPPED SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING A FEW TORNADOES...DAMAGING GUSTS...AND ISOLATED LARGE HAIL. THERE WILL BE SOME POTENTIAL FOR STORMS TO CONGEAL INTO A MORE SOLID LINE LATER THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...WITH A CONTINUED DAMAGING WIND RISK INTO WRN IL. INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS...CONVECTION WILL WEAKEN AS ALREADY MARGINAL BUOYANCY FURTHER DIMINISHES WITH EWD EXTENT.

sections.title: ARKLATEX THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: LOW-MID 70S BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS ARE SPREADING NWD/NEWD TOWARD THE ARKLATEX AS OF MID MORNING. LAPSE RATES ALOFT ARE NOT PARTICULARLY STEEP AND LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL BE WEAKER COMPARED TO AREAS FARTHER NE IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE SURFACE LOW. STILL...A FEW CLOUD BREAKS AND THE RICH MOISTURE COULD BOOST MLCAPE TO 1000-1500 J/KG BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON ACROSS E/NE TX...WITH SOMEWHAT WEAKER BUOYANCY EXPECTED FARTHER TO THE NE INTO SRN AR. A FEW STORMS SHOULD FORM THIS AFTERNOON ALONG THE REMNANT DRYLINE/CONFLUENCE BAND WHICH WILL APPROACH THE ARKLATEX FROM THE W...AND CONVECTION WILL SUBSEQUENTLY MOVE NEWD INTO THIS EVENING. DEEP-LAYER SHEAR AND BUOYANCY WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELLS...WITH AT LEAST SOME RISK FOR A TORNADO OR TWO...IN ADDITION TO A FEW DAMAGING GUSTS.

sections.title: SRN MO/NRN AR THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: VERTICAL SHEAR PROFILES WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS ALONG THE REMNANT DRYLINE FROM NW AR INTO SW MO THIS AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...BUOYANCY IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN QUITE MARGINAL AS A RESULT OF THE STEEPER LAPSE RATES REMAINING FARTHER N...THE RICHER MOISTURE REMAINING FARTHER S...AND CLOUDS LIMITING SURFACE HEATING. THUS...ATTEMPTS AT SURFACE-BASED CONVECTION MAY END UP BEING OVERWHELMED BY THE VERY STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR ACROSS THIS AREA. WILL MAINTAIN LOW WIND/TORNADO PROBABILITIES TO REFLECT THE CONDITIONAL SEVERE RISK...BUT THE OVERALL SEVERE/SUPERCELL RISK SHOULD REMAIN MARGINAL. ..THOMPSON/PICCA.. 11/11/2015

outlooks.summary: STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS REMAIN A THREAT DURING THE AFTERNOON ACROSS PARTS OF THE MISSOURI VALLEY SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO EASTERN TEXAS. THE GREATEST CONCENTRATION OF POTENTIALLY SEVERE STORMS THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING SHOULD EXIST ACROSS PARTS OF IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI INTO NORTHERN AND CENTRAL ILLINOIS.

sections.title: PARTS OF ERN NEB/NERN KS/WRN IA
sections.text: BASED ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS AND THE ARRIVAL OF STRONG DEEP-LAYER ASCENT/DPVA...CURRENTLY SPREADING INTO NORTHWEST MO AND SOUTHWEST IA HAS RESULTED IN MINOR CHANGES IN THE SPATIAL EXTENT OF THE SLIGHT AND MARGINAL SEVERE WEATHER RISK AREAS IN NERN KS...ERN NEB AND A PART OF WRN IA. THIS COMBINED WITH THE WWD ADVANCEMENT OF HIGHER SURFACE DEW POINTS /LOWER-MID 50S INTO MORE OF WRN/NWRN IA/ AND TRACK OF A DEEPENING SURFACE LOW IN FAR SOUTHEAST NEB...TRACKING THROUGH WRN IA THIS AFTERNOON...FURTHER SUPPORTS THE EXPANSION OF THE SLIGHT AND MARGINAL SEVERE WEATHER RISK AREAS. GENERAL TSTM AREA WAS ALSO ADJUSTED ACROSS EASTERN KS AND WESTERN NEB FOR THE EASTWARD MOVEMENT OF THE UPPER TROUGH. REFER TO VALID SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS FOR THE SEVERE RISK AREAS.

sections.title: ELSEWHERE
sections.text: THE FORECAST REASONING FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE OUTLOOK AREAS IS ON TRACK...WITH NO CHANGES NEEDED WITH THIS OUTLOOK ISSUANCE. ..PETERS.. 11/11/2015 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1023 AM CST WED NOV 11 2015/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SURFACE-BASED STORMS SHOULD COMMENCE AROUND MIDDAY ALONG A COLD FRONT ACROSS THE LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY. ALL SEVERE HAZARDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THIS ACTIVITY AS IT MOVES RAPIDLY NORTH TO EAST THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. A MARGINAL SEVERE HAIL THREAT ALSO EXISTS WITH ELEVATED STORMS NORTHWEST OF THE WARM SECTOR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 16Z SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACED A PAIR OF 995 MB CYCLONES OVER N-CNTRL KS. LEADING PACIFIC COLD FRONT/EFFECTIVE DRYLINE HAS REACHED ERN KS WITH AGITATED CU ALONG IT. THE CYCLONES SHOULD CONSOLIDATE AS THEY TRACK NE ALONG A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT ACROSS FAR SERN NEB INTO SWRN AND W-CNTRL IA THIS AFTERNOON. MODEL FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST 55-57 DEG F SURFACE DEW POINTS WILL BE THE DELIMITER FOR MEAGER SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY. THIS MOISTURE PLUME SHOULD SHIFT NE FROM THE LOWER MO VALLEY ACROSS NRN MO TO CNTRL IA. AS THE LEFT-EXIT REGION OF THE POWERFUL MID-LEVEL JET OVERSPREADS THE NRN PERIPHERY OF THE CONFINED WARM SECTOR...COOLING ALOFT WILL AID IN STEEPENING MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND YIELD WEAKENING MLCIN /EVIDENT IN THE 12Z TOP RAOB/ AMID ONLY WEAK DIABATIC SURFACE HEATING. SURFACE-BASED TSTMS SHOULD INITIATE BY 18-19Z INVOF THE NEB/KS/MO BORDER AREA. ORIENTATION OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR TO THE FRONT AND ENLARGED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR FAST-MOVING LOW-TOPPED SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELL STRUCTURES /ESPECIALLY ACROSS SRN IA AND NRN MO/. FARTHER NW...ARCS OF ELEVATED CONVECTION WILL POSE A MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL RISK...BUT THIS THREAT SHOULD BE SPATIALLY CONFINED AND DIMINISH WITH NRN EXTENT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: MONITORING FOR A POTENTIAL EXTENSION OF THE TORNADO RISK TO THE N OF WW 354 AS THE WARM SECTOR HAS BACKED WEST INTO PARTS OF THE OMAHA METRO AREA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SUPERCELL NOW INTO CASS COUNTY IN SERN NEB AS OF 1830Z APPEARS TO BE JUST AHEAD OF A 993 MB CYCLONE NEAR THE SERN NEB/NERN KS BORDER. THE QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT THAT THE SURFACE LOW WILL TRACK ALONG THIS AFTERNOON HAS BACKED SLIGHTLY WWD OVER THE PAST HOUR AND APPEARS TO BE BISECTING PORTIONS OF THE OMAHA METRO AREA. IT IS PLAUSIBLE THAT THIS SUPERCELL AND/OR ADDITIONAL STORMS TO THE N MAY MAINTAIN SURFACE-BASED CHARACTER AS THEY AFFECT PORTIONS OF SARPY/DOUGLAS COUNTIES IN NEB AND MONONA COUNTY IA THROUGH 21Z. ..GRAMS.. 11/11/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TORNADO THREAT SHOULD INCREASE AND PEAK IN THE 21-00Z TIME FRAME AS STORMS IN AN ARCING BAND ATTEMPT TO DEVELOP EMBEDDED SUPERCELL STRUCTURES.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 19Z SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACED A 991 MB CYCLONE NEAR OMAHA WITH DRYLINE EXTENDING S TOWARDS THE WRN KANSAS CITY METRO AREA. CONVECTION ALONG THE DRYLINE HAS STRUGGLED TO GREATLY INTENSIFY OVER THE PAST HOUR...BUT SHOULD TURN THE CORNER AND DEVELOP SUPERCELL STRUCTURES DURING THE NEXT HOUR AS THE PEAK COMBO OF INSTABILITY/SHEAR/FORCING BECOMES PRESENT. CLOUD BREAKS AHEAD OF THE BAND HAVE SUPPORTED SURFACE TEMPERATURES WARMING INTO THE MIDDLE 60S TO MIDDLE 70S ACROSS NRN MO...YIELDING MEAGER MLCAPE TO AROUND 500 J/KG. HIGHLY ELONGATED HODOGRAPHS SAMPLED IN THE 18Z TOP RAOB AND AREA VWP DATA AMID ROBUST SURFACE PRESSURE FALLS NEAR 3 MB/HR IN THE LEFT-EXIT REGION OF AN INTENSE MID-LEVEL JET SHOULD FAVOR FAST-MOVING CONVECTION WITH A RISK FOR ALL SEVERE HAZARDS CONTINUING INTO EARLY EVENING. ..GRAMS.. 11/11/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PREDOMINANT DAMAGING WIND AND A TEMPORALLY LIMITED TORNADO THREAT SHOULD DEVELOP E OF WW 534 TOWARDS THE MID-MS VALLEY THIS EVENING. WHILE WATCH TYPE IS UNCLEAR...ADDITIONAL WW ISSUANCE IS LIKELY BY 22Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BAND OF ARCING TSTMS ALONG THE DRYLINE HAS INTENSIFIED IN THE PAST HALF HOUR WITH EMBEDDED SUPERCELL STRUCTURES AND SHORT-LINE SEGMENTS. CURRENT FORWARD SPEED IS AROUND 50 KT WHICH PLACES THE MO PORTION OF THE FRONTAL BAND NEAR THE ERN EDGE OF WW 534 AROUND 2230Z. AS THE CONVECTION OCCLUDES THE NRN EXTENT OF UPPER 50S SURFACE DEW POINTS IN CNTRL MO...OVERALL INTENSITY SHOULD PEAK WITHIN WW 534. HOWEVER...THE PRESENCE OF INTENSE MID-LEVEL SWLYS SEMI-PERPENDICULAR TO THE ORIENTATION OF THE TSTM BAND...A RISK FOR AT LEAST DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD PERSIST TO THE MS RIVER. AN APPRECIABLE TORNADO RISK SHOULD REMAIN TEMPORALLY CONFINED TO ABOUT AN HOUR OR TWO AFTER SUNSET AS THE LIMITED SURFACE INSTABILITY FURTHER WANES...A SCENARIO WELL SUPPORTED BY CAM GUIDANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS WILL SLOWLY ORGANIZE THROUGH EARLY EVENING OVER THE MCD AREA...WITH AN INCREASING RISK FOR STRONG/SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF A FEW DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. WW ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE WITHIN THE NEXT FEW HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 20Z SFC ANALYSIS/RADAR IMAGERY PLACE A SFC TROUGH/FRONT STRETCHING FROM FAR SERN OK SWWD ACROSS THE ERN DFW METROPLEX AND TOWARDS THE TX HILL COUNTRY. TO ITS EAST...FAIRLY RICH BL MOISTURE CONTINUES TO STREAM NWD IN WEAKLY CONFLUENT FLOW. SHOWERS/THUNDERSTORMS HAVE BEEN CONTINUALLY FORMING NEAR/AHEAD OF THE SFC BOUNDARY...BUT SO FAR RADAR IMAGERY SUGGESTS UPDRAFTS HAVE BEEN STRUGGLING TO OVERCOME A HIGH SHEAR/LOW BUOYANCY IMBALANCE. NONETHELESS...PERSISTENT NWD MOISTURE TRANSPORT /E.G. SFC DEW POINTS IN THE LOWER 70S IN NERN TX AND SRN AR/...INSOLATION AHEAD OF THE BOUNDARY...AND MOISTENING/COOLING BENEATH THE RIGHT-ENTRANCE OF A MID-LEVEL JET OVERSPREADING THE OZARKS SHOULD BE ENOUGH TO SUSTAIN GREATER THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE. INDEED...RECENT KFWS DATA INDICATE MORE VIGOROUS UPDRAFT DEVELOPMENT MAY BE UNDERWAY. AS STORMS GRADUALLY ORGANIZE THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE ARKLATEX/VICINITY WITH THE APPROACH OF THE FRONT...A TENDENCY FOR VEERING SFC WINDS SHOULD BE OFFSET SOME BY AMPLE SPEED SHEAR. THUS...DESPITE WEAKER LOW-LEVEL FLOW RELATIVE TO POINTS NORTH...THE RISK FOR A COUPLE OF TORNADOES AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL SLOWLY INCREASE...ESPECIALLY WHERE CLOUD BREAKS HAVE BEEN MORE PROMINENT. OTHERWISE...MEAGER LOW/MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES SHOULD FAVOR RELATIVELY LOW-TOPPED CONVECTION...WITH ABUNDANT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR SUPPORTING SOME ELONGATED SUPERCELLULAR STRUCTURES. FURTHERMORE...SHEAR ORIENTATION RELATIVE TO THE SFC FRONT MAY FAVOR A MIX OF DISCRETE CELLS AND SMALL LINEAR SEGMENTS AS CELLS SPREAD EAST. CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE WW ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AT LEAST A MARGINAL RISK OF MAINLY A FEW STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS MIGHT EVOLVE INTO EXTREME NERN IA AND SWRN WI. A WW WILL PROBABLY NOT BE NECESSARY UNLESS CONVECTIVE TRENDS BEGIN TO DICTATE OTHERWISE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AN ORGANIZED LINE OF THUNDERSTORMS WITH EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENTS AND SUPERCELLS LOCATED FROM ECNTRL IA SWD INTO NERN MO IS MOVING RAPIDLY ENEWD AT AROUND 40 KT. THIS STRONGLY FORCED BAND OF STORMS IS DEVELOPING WITHIN ZONE OF STRONG DPVA AND LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE IN EXIT REGION OF A STRONG MID-LEVEL JET. COOL AIR ALOFT NORTH OF UPPER JET AXIS IS SUPPORTING A POCKET OF STEEPER MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND MARGINAL INSTABILITY. THE STRONGEST STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO REMAIN CONFINED TO WW 535 FROM ECNTRL AND SERN IA INTO WCNTRL IL. THE NEAR-SFC LAYER IS MORE STABLE FROM NERN IA INTO SWRN WI WHERE DEWPOINTS ARE ONLY AROUND 50 F WELL NORTH OF A WARM FRONT...SUGGESTING NRN END OF LINE WILL PROBABLY BEGIN TO WEAKEN IS IT MOVES INTO THE MORE STABLE REGIME OF EXTREME NERN IA AND SWRN WI. NEVERTHELESS...AT LEAST A LOW-END RISK FOR STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND WILL EXIST IN THIS AREA EARLY THIS EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THOUGH OVERALL SEVERE THREAT MAY UNDERGO AT LEAST A MODEST DECREASE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS...SOME THREAT FOR PRIMARILY DAMAGING WIND IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST EAST OF WW 535 INTO NRN AND CNTRL IL AND POSSIBLY EXTREME SRN WI. THEREFORE...ANOTHER WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED BEFORE 01Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF ORGANIZED STORMS WITH EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENTS PERSISTS FROM ERN IA THROUGH EXTREME WRN IL INTO NERN MO MOVING EAST AT 35-40 KT. THIS BAND OF STORMS WILL CONTINUE DEVELOPING WITHIN ZONE OF STRONG FORCING ALOFT/DPVA AND LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE ASSOCIATED WITH A PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ITS ATTENDANT MID-LEVEL AND LOW-LEVEL JETS. SFC LOW IS EXPECTED TO UNDERGO FURTHER DEEPENING WITH STRONG PRESSURE FALLS AS IT MOVES NEWD TOWARD SWRN WI. DESPITE THE PRESENCE OF A MORE STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER WITH EWD EXTENT INTO IL...COLD AIR ALOFT NORTH OF UPPER JET AXIS AND MODEST LOW-LEVEL THETA-E ADVECTION ALONG THE STRENGTHENING SLY LLJ WILL CONTRIBUTE TO AT LEAST WEAK NWD DESTABILIZATION WITH TIME. THOUGH THE PRIMARY THREAT WILL BE DAMAGING WIND...A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED STRONG WIND GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE AS A LINE OF TSTMS MOVES EWD INTO THE REGION BUT LIMITED INSTABILITY IS EXPECTED TO TEMPER THE OVERALL THREAT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACES A PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH FROM ADF /IN CNTRL AR/ SWWD TO JUST W OF EDC /IN CNTRL TX/. TSTM ACTIVITY HAS PERSISTED ALONG AND/OR JUST N OF THIS BOUNDARY AS IT PUSHES EWD ACROSS THE REGION. AIRMASS AHEAD OF THIS TROUGH IS QUITE WARM AND MOIST WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S AND TEMPERATURES IN THE MID TO UPPER 70S. MOST RECENT MESOANALYSIS ESTIMATES MLCAPE BETWEEN 500 AND 1000 J PER KG. RECENT 00Z SHV SOUNDING SAMPLED MLCAPE AROUND 700 J PER KG. HOWEVER...TEMPERATURES WILL GRADUALLY DECREASE WITH THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING WITH MUCH OF THE INSTABILITY EXPECTED TO DECREASE AS WELL. BASED ON REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY...TSTMS HAVE STRUGGLED TO MAINTAIN STRONG UPDRAFTS...LIKELY THE RESULT OF AN UNDERCUTTING BOUNDARY...NEUTRAL LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT...AND WARM AIR ALOFT /AROUND 700 MB BASED ON THE 00Z SHV SOUNDING/. THE TREND OF TRANSIENT UPDRAFT STRENGTH IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST...PARTICULARLY GIVEN THE DECREASING SURFACE TEMPERATURES AND RESULTING DECREASE IN SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY. AS A RESULT...DESPITE STRONG KINEMATIC FIELDS...THE OVERALL SVR THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN ISOLATED WITH A FEW STRONG WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE. TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED CLOSELY BUT A WW IS NOT ANTICIPATED AT THIS TIME.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND WILL PERSIST OVER NERN IL THROUGH 0330Z. BASED ON CURRENT MOVEMENT...SQUALL LINE WILL APPROACH THE CHICAGO AREA NEAR 03Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A DECREASING TREND IN LIGHTNING AND STORM TOP HEIGHTS HAS BEEN OBSERVED DURING THE PAST HOUR. HOWEVER...THE SQUALL LINE EXTENDING FROM NERN THROUGH CNTRL IL REMAINS ORGANIZED WITH A FEW BOWING SEGMENTS STILL OBSERVED. THE LINE IS MOVING EAST AT 40 KT AND WILL APPROACH THE CHICAGO METRO AREA BY 03Z. A 61 KT WIND GUST WAS RECENTLY REPORTED AT THE PEORIA ASOS...AND LATEST CHICAGO VWP INDICATES A 75 KT SLY LLJ. DESPITE A LIKELY SLOW BUT GRADUAL WEAKENING OF SQUALL LINE DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...THREAT FOR ISOLATED STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE AS HIGHER MOMENTUM AIR IS TRANSFERRED DOWN TO THE SFC LAYER WITHIN THE CONVECTIVE BAND. ..DIAL.. 11/12/2015 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A STRONG TO DAMAGING CONVECTIVE WIND GUST CANNOT BE RULED OUT AS THE WEAKENING LINE OF STORMS CONTINUES INTO THE GREAT LAKES AREA. HOWEVER...OVERALL THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN TOO MARGINAL FOR A WW ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LOW-TOPPED LINE OF SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE CHICAGO AREA SWD INTO ERN IL CONTINUES EWD AT NEAR 40 KT. SOME BOWING AND LEWP SEGMENTS CONTINUE TO BE OBSERVED...AND THE LLJ IS STRENGTHENING OVER THE UPPER GREAT LAKES. HOWEVER...THE DOWNSTREAM NEAR-SFC LAYER IS STABLE WITH LIMITED INSTABILITY. STRONG FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH THE PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ITS COUPLED JET STRUCTURE SHOULD MAINTAIN THE SHALLOW CONVECTIVE BAND NEXT COUPLE HOURS. WHILE SOME DOWNWARD MOMENTUM TRANSFER REMAINS POSSIBLE WITHIN PORTIONS OF THE LINE...THE VERY MARGINAL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT SHOULD SERVE AS AN OVERALL LIMITING FACTOR FOR A MORE ROBUST SEVERE THREAT.
